title: I Posted the Gold-Panning Trough Hours After They Took My Numbered Sluice

parts.text: I set my pan at trough two at 9:05 a.m. and member Tor was already rocking our numbered sluice. The board said: ONE TROUGH. NINETY MINUTES. SLUICE STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was fifty-two, club member, holding a claim card that listed our gravel. Tor shrugged. "Members are the creek." I photographed the board, the booking, and his classifier on our riffles. Then I asked for the trough log. At 9:13 the creek pinged why Tor's name was on our sluice. I kept my voice creek-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A board is only a board until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The creek can see Tor's classifier on our riffles during our booking.

social.video_title: He rocked our numbered sluice on our trough — Part 1/2
social.description: Gold trough, a member on our riffles, a ninety-minute board he posted. I logged the classifier. Would you have asked for the trough log?

parts.text: Tor called it a rinse until the creek asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the classifier still. The sluice went back to our peg. Tor ran his own ninety and told the next member atmosphere was always about color. Color is a word members use when a booking exists. Trough policy now has a second line: MEMBERS ARE NOT THE CREEK. I keep our sluice on a labeled hook. Tor brown-bags his jokes. The creek finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Members are not the creek — Part 2/2
social.description: Trough log, numbered sluice, and a second line on the board. Was a rinse ever our riffles?
